# Messages and errors

The agent talks back asynchronously with messages. `fridamj` drains them:

```text
[0x00000000]> fridamj
{"ok":true,"result":{"messages":[...],"dropped":0}}
```

## The kinds

| Kind | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `send` | a payload from `send()` or an agent event | `{"type":"agent.ready","version":1}`, `frida.bp`, `frida.wp`, `frida.rn` |
| `log` | console output | `console.log`, `console.error` |
| `error` | an uncaught script error | description + stack |
| `unknown` | anything the host cannot classify | rare |

**console.log** becomes a `log` message:

```text
[0x00000000]> fridaej "console.log('from console')"
{"ok":true,"result":{"value":null,"type":"undefined"}}

[0x00000000]> fridamj
... {"kind":"log","level":"info","text":"from console"}
```

**console.error** keeps the level:

```text
... {"kind":"log","level":"error","text":"to stderr"}
```

**An exception thrown inside an eval** is not a message: the eval request
itself fails:

```text
[0x00000000]> fridaej "throw new Error('boom')"
{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"internal_error","message":"boom"}}
```

**An exception in asynchronous code** (a timer, a callback) cannot fail a
request, so it becomes an `error` message with a stack:

```text
[0x00000000]> fridaej "setTimeout(function(){throw new Error('async boom')},300)"
{"ok":true,"result":{"value":1,"type":"number"}}

[0x00000000]> fridamj
... {"kind":"error","description":"Error: async boom","stack":"Error: async boom\n    at eval (undefined:1:29)\n    at /frida/runtime/core.js:55:14"}
```

![Message kinds](img/scripting/message-kinds.png)

## Binary payloads

`send()` with a binary second argument arrives base64-encoded with its
size:

```text
[0x00000000]> fridaej "send('binary-payload',[1,2,3,255])"
{"ok":true,"result":{"value":null,"type":"undefined"}}

[0x00000000]> fridamj
... {"kind":"send","payload":"binary-payload","data":"AQID/w==","dataSize":4}
```

`AQID/w==` decodes to `01 02 03 ff`.

## The buffer

The buffer holds up to 256 messages on the host side. When it overflows,
the oldest messages are dropped and the count is reported:

```text
{"ok":true,"result":{"messages":[...],"dropped":3}}
```

Drain regularly, as the earlier chapters do, and treat `dropped` as a sign
that the target is noisier than your last drain.

> **Note:** buffering is host-side: the agent always delivers. The host
> keeps the newest 256.

::: {.callout-tip}
### Try

Log with `console.log` and `console.error`, throw inside a `setTimeout`,
and `send` a binary payload. Drain everything and classify each message.
:::
